title: References vs pointers
body: Which statement about C++ references is true?

options.t: A reference must be initialised, cannot be null in valid code and cannot be reseated to refer to another object

explanation: Use references for required parameters and pointers (or std::optional) when 'no object' is a valid state.

title: RAII

options.t: Tying resource lifetime to object lifetime: acquire in the constructor, release in the destructor

explanation: Destructors run deterministically at scope exit, even during exceptions, so smart pointers, lock_guard and file wrappers never leak.

title: unique_ptr vs shared_ptr
body: Which statement about smart pointers is correct?

options.t: unique_ptr has sole ownership and can only be moved; shared_ptr uses reference counting for shared ownership

answer: unique_ptr = exclusive, movable; shared_ptr = shared, ref-counted.
explanation: Prefer unique_ptr by default (zero overhead). Break shared_ptr cycles with weak_ptr. Create them with make_unique / make_shared.

title: Virtual destructors
body: Why should a polymorphic base class declare a virtual destructor?

options.t: Deleting a derived object through a base pointer otherwise has undefined behaviour and the derived destructor does not run

answer: So delete via a base pointer calls the derived destructor.
explanation: Rule of thumb: if a class has any virtual functions, give it a public virtual destructor (or a protected non-virtual one).
